title: Evolution and Natural Selection
seo_title: Grade 7 Science: Evolution and Natural Selection Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Evolution by natural selection provides an explanation for the diversity and survival of living things: variation, survival of the fittest, natural selection, and the fossil record as evidence. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 7, Biology)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 science worksheets (BC): variation, adaptation, natural selection, evidence for evolution, and artificial selection. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things best suited to their environment survive.
key_sub: Variation, selection and inheritance over many generations.
body_html:
How to think about it

Members of a species vary. Some variations help an organism survive and reproduce in its environment. These organisms pass the useful traits to their offspring, so over many generations the population changes. This is natural selection.

Evidence for evolution includes fossils, similar body structures in different species, and DNA. People use artificial selection to breed plants and animals with traits they want.

Example

Bacteria that resist an antibiotic survive and multiply. What is this an example of?

The environment chose which ones lived.

Answer: natural selection

Example

Who chooses the traits in artificial selection?

Think of dog breeds.

Answer: people

Common mistakes

  • Thinking an individual changes to survive (populations change over generations).
  • Thinking 'fittest' means strongest.
  • Thinking evolution happens on purpose.

items.q: Natural selection: “Those best suited to the environment are more likely to survive.” What happens next?

The survivors breed and pass on their useful characteristics.
Animals of one kind vary: some are slightly different from others.
Over many generations, the useful characteristic becomes common.
items.e: Variation → change → survival → breeding → many generations.
